content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm attempting to log into the [product_name] over the internet using a [product_name] communication module. My initial approach was to connect using openvpn, but our SIM cards have private IP addresses, making this method unavailable. In the security settings of the [product_name] device, I enabled HTTPS. Now, I can access the [product_name] module using the IP address provided by our carrier, but I must first establish a VPN connection via Cisco AnyConnect. My current challenge is accessing the [product_name] and determining what IP address I should use. The network settings indicate that the gateway is set to the LAN address of the [product_name] communication module. Am I overlooking something? Any suggestions would be appreciated. Update: After revisiting the manual several times, I found that connecting to the [product_name] via HTTPS is not supported. I will continue searching for alternative solutions, possibly figuring out how to use openvpn.
Which firmware version does your [product_name] communication module have? Which exact model of [product_name] do you have? Please provide the full [article_no].
Thank you for your quick reply. We have the latest [product_name], [article_no]. Firmware version of the [product_name] communication module is [version_no].
Are you familiar with this application example from [company_name]? It covers setting up a secure VPN connection between a PC and [product_name].

Yes, I've tried all the steps mentioned in that application to establish a connection, but nothing has worked. Today, I managed to connect using openvpn through two VPN connections, but it didn't help. Using the openvpn IP address results in a timeout error. I'm considering obtaining a SIM card with a public IP address to see if that resolves the issue. However, I still believe it should be possible to connect over VPN, so I'll keep trying. Update 29-06: Although I now have an openvpn connection, I'm unable to log into the web interface of the [product_name] communication module, which also prevents access to the [product_name]. I'm currently stuck. If anyone has other suggestions, please let me know.
Is it possible to enable port forwarding or open specific ports on the [product_name] communication module?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering difficulty accessing the [product_name] remotely over HTTPS via the [product_name] communication module, especially when using VPN and SIM cards with private IPs. The web interface for [product_name] cannot be reached as expected through VPN—timeouts occur and connectivity needs remain unmet. Documentation confirms that HTTPS access to the [product_name] is not possible, resulting in user frustration and workflow interruption.
